title: Is it legal to train AI models on copyrighted books? It’s complicated
slides: Can AI legally learn from your copyrighted book?
Courts haven't settled this; lawsuits are pending.
Fair use might protect AI, but no ruling yet.
Your writing could train competitors without consent.
Act now: register works and monitor AI outputs.
thread_text:
1. Your book, their AI

A federal court just allowed a copyright lawsuit against AI training to proceed, but no final verdict yet.

2. The fair use gamble

Fair use could let AI train on your work, but judges disagree on whether it applies to massive datasets.

3. The silent competitor

Your manuscript could quietly be used to train a rival author's AI-writing tool without you ever knowing.

4. What you can do now

Register your works with the copyright office and set up alerts to check if AI outputs quote your prose.

5. Test your own risk

Ask ChatGPT to mimic your latest chapter. If it's close, would you sue? Decide this week.

instagram.caption:
Your novel could end up as training data for an AI writing tool—and right now, no court has definitively said that’s illegal. ⚖️

Lawsuits are pending, but judges haven’t settled whether “fair use” protects companies scraping entire books. That means publishers and authors are stuck in legal limbo while AI models keep learning from their work.

For you, this isn’t abstract: your manuscript might quietly teach a competitor’s AI to mimic your style without your permission.

Register your copyrights today, then run a test—ask an AI chatbot to finish a paragraph from your draft. If it sounds close to yours, would you sue? 

🔍📚✍️
